title: Sitting in at the Onyx Club and being hired by John Kirby
summary: After a Joe Louis fight, he dropped into the Onyx Club, borrowed Pete Brown's horn to play Maxine Sullivan's set and was hired on the spot; tone mattered behind a singer.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Cotton Club, you know, and be seen around there, and talking and whatever. You know. So one night -- one night my wife and I, we were downtown. We had just come from a fight. We went to see Joe Louis fight in Madison Square Garden. He fought a fellow named Nathan Mann who he knocked out in the second or third round or something like that. So I -- so we walked down, you know, walking down the street, and we got to 52nd Street. So then when we got to 52nd Street where Kirby was working at the Onyx Club. So I said to my wife, I said, "I think I'll -- come on, let's go in here to the Onyx Club."
"No, you go in," she said. "I think I'll go home." I remember distinctly, you know. So she says, "Oh, yes, Kirby's in there." So she said, "Well, you go ahead. I'm going home."

So I went in the Onyx Club and talked to Kirby, you know, not actually looking for a job, you know. I wanted to hear his band because they used to broadcast and I used to hear him on the radio, so I wanted to see it. So I went in. So Kirby said to me -- Maxine is getting ready to go on, so he said, "Why don't you come on and play Maxine's music." So Pete Brown was the alto player, so I took -- it was all right with Pete. You know, in those days you'd sit in. So I was just sitting in. So he loaned me his horn and I played the set with Maxine and it went over pretty big, you know. So Kirby, he hired me on the spot right then.

Yeah. And it was a thing that it was just a complete turnaround, because Pete Brown, as I say, in those days tone was the thing, you know.
